pathway.title: CNX Resources Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage and cover are low on every measure the sources support, but reported ratios swing with hedge marks. Net debt was 1.25x reported EBITDA and 1.80x adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 4.16x on reported EBITDA at FY2024, when derivative losses depressed earnings. The adjusted measure is the steadier guide to debt service, and on it cash interest is covered 7.99x. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Liquidity is strong and rests on undrawn revolvers, not cash. Cash was USD 1.98 million, and undrawn capacity was USD 1,673.05 million, of which USD 533 million belongs to the midstream subsidiary's facility alone; both revolvers mature on 2029-05-17 and no principal falls due before FY2029. The consequence is that near-term obligations are covered by committed lines, with the 2029 revolver maturity the first test. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Earnings are tied to one commodity in one basin, hedged most heavily for 2026. Natural gas is 92% of sales volumes and the issuer states that 82% of expected 2026 gas volumes are hedged, so cash flow is best protected in 2026 and more exposed later. Fixed gas transportation and processing commitments of USD 1,237.86 million raise operating leverage if prices or volumes fall. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Capital return is the policy risk. Repurchases of USD 432.78 million in the nine months exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 402.61 million, and net revolver borrowings of USD 67.10 million covered the excess; no dividend is paid. The consequence is that leverage depends on a board choice, with USD 1,991.71 million of repurchase authority still open. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Market access was demonstrated in 2026 and maturities were extended. The company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due March 2034 and repurchased USD 500 million of senior notes due January 2029, and settled the convertible notes in shares. The consequence is a ladder with USD 299.85 million due in FY2029 and the notes beginning in FY2030. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: Independent natural gas development, production, midstream and technology company centred in the Appalachian Basin, with Marcellus and Utica shale operations in three states and coalbed methane in Virginia

runs.text: The first strength is low leverage and wide cover, because net debt of 1.80x adjusted EBITDA and cash interest cover of 7.99x leave room to absorb an earnings fall before debt service is stressed. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second strength is liquidity depth and distant maturities, because USD 1,673.05 million of undrawn revolver capacity and no principal before FY2029 mean obligations are covered by committed lines. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The third strength is demonstrated market access, because the 2026 issue of notes due March 2034 and the repurchase of notes due January 2029 extended the ladder, and the convertible notes were settled in shares, not cash. Basis: calculation C5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fourth strength is hedge-protected 2026 cash flow and a modest unit cost, because 82% of expected 2026 gas volumes are hedged and lifting cost was $0.15 per Mcfe against a realised price of $2.75 per Mcfe in FY2025. Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth strength is an owned gathering system and an operated reserve base, because 99.1% of reserves are operated and 72.2% proved developed, which gives control over development timing and takeaway. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cnx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is single-commodity, single-basin exposure with earnings that swing on hedge marks, because natural gas is 92% of volumes and FY2024 reported leverage of 4.16x fell to 1.25x as hedge marks moved from losses to gains. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second weakness is capital return above free cash flow, because USD 432.78 million of repurchases exceeded USD 402.61 million of free cash flow and the shortfall was met from the revolver. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The third weakness is fixed commitments, because USD 1,237.86 million of gas transportation and processing obligations persist if volumes fall. Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

The fourth weakness is legacy coal liabilities that depend on Core's indemnity, because a USD 75 million settlement is reimbursed by Core and a Coal Act suit remains with no accrual. Basis: calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth weakness is incomplete evidence on priority and control, because the debt documents, proxy statement and ratings are not supplied and USD 467.00 million of midstream debt sits outside the parent's guarantee. Basis: calculation C12; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The company's 2026 debt activity was a refinancing, not new leverage. In February 2026 it issued USD 500 million of senior notes due March 2034 at par under an indenture dated 2026-02-26, guaranteed by the restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the CNX credit facility, and during the nine months it repurchased all USD 500 million of senior notes due January 2029 at 101.6% of principal for USD 507.97 million, recording a USD 12.01 million loss on extinguishment. The CNX credit facility borrowing base and elected commitments were unchanged at the 2026-05-13 redetermination. Basis: calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

The equity-linked debt was removed without cash. On 2025-12-15 the company exchanged about USD 122.10 million of convertible notes for shares, and on 2026-05-01 the remaining USD 208.55 million of principal matured and was settled in newly issued shares, with the capped call transactions expiring and their shares retired. No convertible notes remain outstanding. Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

Acquisitions and disposals were modest and are funded from operating cash flow and the revolver. The Apex Energy II acquisition closed on 2025-01-27 for about USD 517.60 million in cash, expanding central Pennsylvania Shale acreage, and the company is paying USD 16.50 million a year for three years for the right to acquire the Utica interests under that footprint; it sold about 7,500 acres of Marcellus rights in Ohio in 2025 for USD 57.09 million and monetised federal tax credits for about USD 30 million on 2026-07-01. Basis: calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

fields.value: CNX Resources Corp (cnx), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and operating model, ownership, governance, capital allocation, transactions and issuer history from the seven supplied filings and the source readiness findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CNX is a scaled, largely hedged Appalachian gas producer with no controlling holder identified, so creditor risk comes from capital-return policy and a legacy coal tail rather than sponsor extraction, though ownership and board facts are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Share repurchases of USD 432.78 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 402.61 million, so leverage can rise without an earnings change, while the 2026 refinancing extended maturities and the convertible notes were settled in shares rather than cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated in one commodity and one basin, but most near-term price exposure is hedged. Natural gas is 92% of sales volumes and the Shale segment is 94% of them, so earnings track Appalachian gas prices; the issuer states that 82% of its expected 2026 gas volumes are hedged. The creditor consequence is that cash flow in 2026 is the best protected and later years carry progressively more price exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital return, not sponsor extraction, is the governance lever that moves creditor risk. The board raised the repurchase authority by USD 2,000 million to USD 4,900 million on 2026-01-29, and the company paid USD 432.78 million to buy back shares in the nine months, USD 30.17 million more than issuer-defined free cash flow; no dividend has been paid since 2016. Net revolver borrowings of USD 67.10 million in the same period covered the excess, so repurchases transmit directly into leverage if they continue at that pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 refinancing was creditor-neutral to positive. The company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due March 2034 in February 2026 and repurchased all USD 500 million of senior notes due January 2029 at 101.6% of principal, extending maturity by five years at a lower coupon and paying a premium of USD 7.97 million, with a loss on extinguishment recorded. The new notes carry the same guarantor scope as the old, and no change in priority is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The legacy coal liabilities are indemnified by Core Natural Resources, not extinguished. The company settled a pension claim for USD 75 million payable over five years and Core has reimbursed every payment so far; a second suit under the Coal Act alleges that both companies are jointly liable, with a loss possible but not probable and no accrual. The credit consequence is counterparty risk on Core's indemnity rather than a balance-sheet liability today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance evidence is thin because the proxy statement is not in the set. Board independence, holder percentages and related-party policy are not established, and the finance officers who signed the July 2026 quarterly report differ from those who signed the October 2026 report with no explanation in the set. Until the proxy statement is read, the absence of a controlling holder is a reading of silence, not a finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading capital return as the main governance risk is balance-sheet room: USD 1,673.05 million of revolver capacity was undrawn at 2026-09-30, and the company used share settlement, not cash, to retire the convertible notes, so buybacks above free cash flow have so far been absorbed without a covenant concern, since compliance with every financial covenant is stated. The view would change toward higher governance risk if the proxy statement shows a holder with control or board rights, if the indentures cap restricted payments in a way that repurchases approach, if repurchases keep exceeding free cash flow while revolver borrowings rise, or if Core disputes its indemnity on the Coal Act suit. It would change toward lower risk if repurchases fall back below free cash flow and the proxy statement shows an independent board with no holder able to direct capital policy.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's 2026 debt activity was a refinancing, not new leverage. In February 2026 it issued USD 500 million of senior notes due March 2034 at par under an indenture dated 2026-02-26, guaranteed by the restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the CNX credit facility, and during the nine months it repurchased all USD 500 million of senior notes due January 2029 at 101.6% of principal for USD 507.97 million, recording a USD 12.01 million loss on extinguishment. The CNX credit facility borrowing base and elected commitments were unchanged at the 2026-05-13 redetermination.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The equity-linked debt was removed without cash. On 2025-12-15 the company exchanged about USD 122.10 million of convertible notes for shares, and on 2026-05-01 the remaining USD 208.55 million of principal matured and was settled in newly issued shares, with the capped call transactions expiring and their shares retired. No convertible notes remain outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and disposals were modest and are funded from operating cash flow and the revolver. The Apex Energy II acquisition closed on 2025-01-27 for about USD 517.60 million in cash, expanding central Pennsylvania Shale acreage, and the company is paying USD 16.50 million a year for three years for the right to acquire the Utica interests under that footprint; it sold about 7,500 acres of Marcellus rights in Ohio in 2025 for USD 57.09 million and monetised federal tax credits for about USD 30 million on 2026-07-01.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CNX Resources Corp (cnx), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: fundamental credit view, strengths and weaknesses, downside path and monitoring triggers, synthesised from the seven supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CNX's credit profile is sound for a gas producer, with low leverage, wide interest cover, ample undrawn liquidity and no principal due before 2029, so near-term creditor risk is low; the main constraint is capital-return policy that has outrun free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At 2026-09-30 net debt was 1.80x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 1.25x reported EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 7.99x, and USD 1,673.05 million of revolver capacity was undrawn against USD 1.98 million of cash. Nine-month share repurchases of USD 432.78 million exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 402.61 million, which is the path by which leverage could rise without an earnings change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and cover are low on every measure the sources support, but reported ratios swing with hedge marks. Net debt was 1.25x reported EBITDA and 1.80x adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 4.16x on reported EBITDA at FY2024, when derivative losses depressed earnings. The adjusted measure is the steadier guide to debt service, and on it cash interest is covered 7.99x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is strong and rests on undrawn revolvers, not cash. Cash was USD 1.98 million, and undrawn capacity was USD 1,673.05 million, of which USD 533 million belongs to the midstream subsidiary's facility alone; both revolvers mature on 2029-05-17 and no principal falls due before FY2029. The consequence is that near-term obligations are covered by committed lines, with the 2029 revolver maturity the first test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are tied to one commodity in one basin, hedged most heavily for 2026. Natural gas is 92% of sales volumes and the issuer states that 82% of expected 2026 gas volumes are hedged, so cash flow is best protected in 2026 and more exposed later. Fixed gas transportation and processing commitments of USD 1,237.86 million raise operating leverage if prices or volumes fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital return is the policy risk. Repurchases of USD 432.78 million in the nine months exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 402.61 million, and net revolver borrowings of USD 67.10 million covered the excess; no dividend is paid. The consequence is that leverage depends on a board choice, with USD 1,991.71 million of repurchase authority still open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Market access was demonstrated in 2026 and maturities were extended. The company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due March 2034 and repurchased USD 500 million of senior notes due January 2029, and settled the convertible notes in shares. The consequence is a ladder with USD 299.85 million due in FY2029 and the notes beginning in FY2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a sound profile is that earnings quality is weaker than the ratios suggest: reported EBITDA of USD 1,820 million over the last twelve months includes unrealised derivative gains of USD 595 million that the issuer removes to reach USD 1,262 million, FY2024 reported leverage of 4.16x shows how fast the ratio moves when hedge marks reverse, and the hedge book thins after 2026 while fixed transport commitments stay. The view would weaken if repurchases keep exceeding free cash flow while revolver borrowings rise, if gas prices fall as hedges roll off, or if Core stops honouring its indemnity on the coal liabilities. It would strengthen if repurchases fall below free cash flow and the executed debt documents show no limit that repurchases approach.

fields.value: The first strength is low leverage and wide cover, because net debt of 1.80x adjusted EBITDA and cash interest cover of 7.99x leave room to absorb an earnings fall before debt service is stressed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is liquidity depth and distant maturities, because USD 1,673.05 million of undrawn revolver capacity and no principal before FY2029 mean obligations are covered by committed lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is demonstrated market access, because the 2026 issue of notes due March 2034 and the repurchase of notes due January 2029 extended the ladder, and the convertible notes were settled in shares, not cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is hedge-protected 2026 cash flow and a modest unit cost, because 82% of expected 2026 gas volumes are hedged and lifting cost was $0.15 per Mcfe against a realised price of $2.75 per Mcfe in FY2025.

fields.value: The fifth strength is an owned gathering system and an operated reserve base, because 99.1% of reserves are operated and 72.2% proved developed, which gives control over development timing and takeaway.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is single-commodity, single-basin exposure with earnings that swing on hedge marks, because natural gas is 92% of volumes and FY2024 reported leverage of 4.16x fell to 1.25x as hedge marks moved from losses to gains.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.value: The second weakness is capital return above free cash flow, because USD 432.78 million of repurchases exceeded USD 402.61 million of free cash flow and the shortfall was met from the revolver.

fields.value: The third weakness is fixed commitments, because USD 1,237.86 million of gas transportation and processing obligations persist if volumes fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CNX is an independent natural gas producer in the Appalachian Basin with owned gathering, producing from Marcellus and Utica shale and Virginia coalbed methane; 92% of sales volumes are natural gas and 94% come from Shale. Its cash flows are therefore a function of regional gas prices, volumes and the hedge book.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and its holders are not established, because the proxy statement is not supplied. Debt sits at two levels: the parent's revolver and notes are guaranteed by most subsidiaries, while the midstream subsidiary's USD 467.00 million of notes and revolver are outside the parent's guarantee and outside the parent's covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cnx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substantially all gas is sold at market prices under short-term contracts, so CNX has no pricing power beyond basis and marketing choices; realised price including hedge settlements was $2.75 per Mcfe in FY2025 against $2.66 per Mcfe in FY2024, and three buyers each took more than 10% of customer revenue in FY2025. The creditor consequence is price-taker revenue with some buyer concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lifting cost was $0.15 per Mcfe in FY2025 against a realised price of $2.75 per Mcfe, but transportation, gathering and compression of USD 383.10 million and fixed firm transport commitments mean a large share of cost does not fall with price. Margins therefore move mainly with price and hedge settlements, which turned from a gain in FY2024 to a loss in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure of USD 451.06 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 took more than half of operating cash flow of USD 810.56 million, leaving USD 359.50 million before asset sale proceeds and issuer-defined free cash flow of USD 402.61 million after them. Conversion is adequate, and the capital programme is guided inside USD 571 million to USD 586 million for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_ex991supplementalq326.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition in a commodity market is on cost and takeaway, where CNX's owned gathering and low lifting cost are advantages; regulation of emissions and pipelines and the climate policy path are the political and environmental pressures the filings name; buyer power is moderate, because gas is sold at market prices to many marketers and utilities, although three buyers each took more than 10% of FY2025 customer revenue. In SWOT terms the strengths are cost, liquidity and access, and the weaknesses are commodity concentration, capital return and legacy liabilities, which the ranked lists above translate into credit terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions the evidence supports these readings: scale and market position average, because output is concentrated in one basin and no peer comparison is supplied; competitive advantage average, resting on lifting cost and owned gathering; business diversification weak, because 92% of volumes are natural gas and 94% come from one segment; cost and capex flexibility average, because capital expenditure is guided inside a range while USD 1,237.86 million of transport commitments are fixed; margin stability average, because hedge marks and price swing reported earnings; free cash flow stability average, because repurchases and asset sales move it; ability to refinance and access capital markets strong, because 2026 issuance extended maturities and no principal is due before FY2029; liquidity position strong, because USD 1,673.05 million is undrawn; and financial policy and governance average, because repurchases exceeded free cash flow while holders are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's 2026 guidance of 612.5 Bcfe to 617.5 Bcfe and hedged volumes support cash flow, while headwinds are the roll-off of hedges, with hedged volumes lower in each year from 2027 to 2029, normal production declines that cut nine-month volumes, and a repurchase pace above free cash flow. Beyond that horizon no source states a plan, so the medium-term view is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_ex991supplementalq326.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a sustained fall in Appalachian gas prices as hedges roll off. Hedged volumes are largest for 2026 and lower in each later year, so the first operational break is lower realised prices on unhedged volumes from 2027. Fixed transport commitments and interest do not fall with price, so EBITDA and free cash flow fall faster than revenue, and leverage rises further if repurchases continue to be funded from the revolver. Liquidity would absorb the shock because USD 1,673.05 million is undrawn and no principal is due before FY2029, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; headroom against the covenant maximum cannot be tested without the executed documents. The observable triggers are realised price below the FY2025 level, free cash flow below repurchases and undrawn capacity below its current level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, CNX presents a sound business and financial profile supported by low leverage, undrawn liquidity and demonstrated market access, but credit quality is constrained by commodity concentration, capital return above free cash flow and legacy coal liabilities. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because hedges cover 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on gas prices and the revolver maturity in 2029. The primary downside path is a gas price fall as hedges roll off while repurchases continue. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the proxy statement and agency ratings. Top risk: capital return funded by the revolver.
